To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) for any WNR and N HR, the best encoding function is scalar QIM with external dithering; 2) for any W NR, the best encoding functions are lattice QIM with external (or internal) dithering and time-sharing, and spread-spectrum with time-sharing, but not lattice QIM without time-sharing; 3) for any W N R, the best encoding family is lattice QIM with internal dithering and external dithering,

(1) the constrained capacity of QIM with external dither is the same as the capacity of spread spectrum; (2) QIM without external dither is better than spread spectrum for all values of WNR and for NHR above 1; (3) QIM without time-sharing is better than spread-spectrum for NHR below 1, but not for NHR above one; (4) the constrained capacity is achieved with a simple encoding scheme that is not time-shared;

the constrained capacity of a Gaussian host is the same for all encoding families that are best under the worst (nonaddative) attack, and that the best encoding family is either scalar QIM, with or without dithering, or higher-dimensional lattice QMI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of Gaussian watermarking with constrained encoding functions, and the results are useful for the design of practical watermarking systems.
a new notion of constrained capacity, and with a new class of improved QIM schemes, which outperform spread-spectrum for Gaussian watermarking.

the following question: what is the best watermark embedding strategy when the attacker is constrained to the worst possible attack, and when the encoder is constrained to lie in a certain family of functions?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for Gaussian host and worst attack, the optimal encoding function lies in a family of lattice QIM schemes with external dithering, time-sharing and high dimension, with the optimal parameters determined in the paper.
lattice QIM with time-sharing and external dithering is best under the best attack for all WNR and N HR.
, for Gaussian watermarking, the best strategy is to use scalar lattice QIM with external dithering, for any admissible WNR and N.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best constrained capacity can be attained with a scalar QIM encoder, followed by lattice QIM, with a time-sharing scheme, and with an appropriate dithering scheme, depending on the value of the WNR.
, in the presence of the worst attack, the best QIM strategy is lattice QIM, with a suitable choice of dithering and time-sharing.
, with the right choice of QIM, the performance of the watermarking system can be made arbitrarily close to the unconstrained capacity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the Gaussian host setting, QIM is the best possible strategy, in the sense that no better strategy exists.
the best QIM schemes for a Gaussian watermarking problem depend on the WNR and N HR, and are not always the same as for the worst additive attack.
QIM can be made to work in a Gaussian setting, and it is the most efficient scheme for the worst attack, even in the high-WNR regime where spread-spectrum is typically preferred.
